text:
maria: FYI — finance flagged an inconsistency between the committed Dedicated pool for Customer Atlas in eu-west-1 and what the cloud invoices show. Can we triage?

chris: what does "committed" look like on our end (units)? GPUs, vCPU-equivalent, or throughput slots?

maria: For Redwood Dedicated we record as 'reserved GPU-equivalent slots' (we normalize different SKUs to a baseline GPU hour). Atlas committed 8 baseline GPUs for the month (8 * 24 * 30 = 5760 GPU-hours).

tom: Cloud invoice shows 10 reserved GPUs for same account/region. That extra 2 -> ~1440 GPU-hours delta.

aly: That delta is ~ $7k/month at current spot/discount mix. Finance opened a ticket because the committed discount doesn't match the billed reservation.

jess: Could this be a provisioning overflow (burst) that was auto-upgraded to on-demand reserved SKU by the cloud provider? I vaguely remember a provider quirk where burst capacity can be billed as reserved if allocation spans the billing cycle change.

chris: Let's check our reservation-to-pool mapping and the autoscaler logs.

maria: I ran the pool mapping: 
```
redwood infra pool show --customer atlas --region eu-west-1 --format table
POOL    CONFIGURED_GPU_EQUIV    ACTIVE_ALLOCS
eu-atl-1    8                      9
```
Looks like one extra active alloc pinned an allocation in that pool.

tom: That "9" active alloc is suspicious — which allocation?

maria: Allocation id: alloc-eu-32 (attached to deployment atlas-search v2).

chris: pull the autoscaler event stream for that alloc window.

maria: pasted events:
```
2026-02-15T03:12Z autoscaler: scaling up +1 due to queued tokens (q=1200)
2026-02-15T03:13Z autoscaler: allocated gpu-pool-slot alloc-eu-32
2026-02-15T03:14Z deploy-bot: canary rollout atlas-search v2 -> traffic 10%
2026-02-15T03:20Z autoscaler: did not scale down (min_pool=8 locked by commit)
```

jess: Ah — canary rollout triggered a short-lived extra allocation that lasted beyond the billing cycle boundary because min_pool was locked by the commit. The provider then attributed that extra allocation to the customer's reserved instances rather than on-demand, which inflated the reserved count.

aly: So the invoice shows 10 reserved GPUs because the provider merges the short allocation with the committed footprint during the billing cutoff. Need to avoid that or get a credit.

chris: Two paths: (1) operational mitigation — ensure short canaries use burst pool not tied to committed slots; (2) finance/contract mitigation — request invoice adjustment for known provider attribution bug.

tom: For (1) we could add a special canary pool flag that allows temporary overcommit without converting to provider-level reservation. Patch proposal: autoscaler honor "canary_burst=true" and put allocations on a separate ephemeral pool with explicit max lifetime (e.g., 2h).

maria: sketching quick config change:
```
pool_policy:
  min_committed: 8
  allow_canary_burst: true
  canary_burst_max_lifetime: "2h"
```
If canary_burst is true, we prefer ephemeral on-demand slots instead of touching committed reservations.

jess: Good idea. Also add a telemetry tag so billing reconciliation can filter ephemeral usage when requesting credits: "rbw:ephemeral=true"

aly: I'll start the finance case with provider support and attach our telemetry + the exact invoice lines. If ops can ensure ephemeral tags appear consistently, we have a stronger case.

chris: Short checklist:
- [ ] patch autoscaler to honor canary_burst (maria/tom)
- [ ] emit billing tags on ephemeral allocs (maria)
- [ ] run replay on last 30 days to see how often this happens (tom)
- [ ] finance ticket + sample invoice lines (aly)

maria: I'm going to prototype the autoscaler change and add a config flag behind a feature gate. Will post PR link.

deploy-bot: Deployment started: infra/autoscaler@canary-burst-feature -> staging

tom: Running a replay now for atlas-prod/eu-west-1 from 2026-01-01 -> 2026-03-01. Preliminary: 3 occurrences where canary/rollout overlapped billing boundary and increased reserved counts.

aly: That's enough to justify asking provider to reclassify 3 reservation spikes. I'll open the support case with the invoice numbers + replay logs.

chris: After autoscaler change, let's add an alert in RedConsole that warns when active_allocs > configured_committed by more than 1 for >1hr near billing cutover (00:00 UTC).

maria: adding alert: 
- name: committed-billing-spike
- condition: active_allocs - configured_committed >= 1 AND time_of_day in [23:30-00:30 UTC] for >1h
- severity: P2

jess: Also update the Dedicated onboarding doc: call out canary_burst strategy and billing gotchas in eu-west-1 (and list provider regions with similar rounding behavior).

aly: I'll keep finance updated. If provider refuses adjustment, we need to evaluate passing discrete credits to Atlas or offering a one-time invoice offset.

maria: Will open PR with config + telemetry and request review from chris/tom. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
